instrument.why: ENFORCEMENT, 'the instrument that produced a claim is part of the claim': a load-bearing claim needs a file-based instrument that has been shown to fail. The claim being made is that the prepared copy is inside the portal's limits and names nothing forbidden. A shell grep would not have been sufficient evidence for that.
instrument.whatItChecks: name <= 100, tagline <= 55, description <= 2000, plus two token lists. HARD tokens must not appear at all. CLAIM tokens are forbidden only when ASSERTED and permitted when denied.
instrument.selfTest: 12 fixtures, run on every invocation, and the script exits 2 if any fixture disagrees. Both directions are covered: 8 must-fail cases AND 4 must-pass cases, so the checker cannot pass by being vacuous.

thirdViolationTest.mutation: Convert the subject file to CRLF line endings.
thirdViolationTest.why: MEMORY records CRLF as a live hazard in this repo, and a fenced-block extractor that anchors on a bare newline is exactly the shape that breaks on it.
thirdViolationTest.history: This was not hypothetical. A patch written by this lane rewrote the pack through Python text mode and turned it CRLF, and the extractor returned ZERO blocks. It crashed loudly on undefined rather than reporting a pass, which is the correct failure direction, but 'crashed' is not 'reported', so the instrument was hardened twice: it now normalizes CRLF before extracting, and it exits 2 with a named reason if fewer than three blocks come out.
thirdViolationTest.expected: exit 0, because a line-ending change must not alter the verdict
thirdViolationTest.observed: exit 0, description 1802/2000, on a file confirmed by `file` to carry CRLF terminators

theCheckerCaughtSomethingRealOnItsFirstR.what: The first version of the checker was presence-shaped and failed the copy on the token 'sold price'. The sentence it flagged was 'It does no valuation, no listings or sold prices, and no owner lookup', which is the sentence that KEEPS the promise rather than breaking it.
theCheckerCaughtSomethingRealOnItsFirstR.whyThisMatters: This is DEV_PROCESS's own lesson arriving inside this lane: a presence-shaped check has one input and cannot tell an assertion from a denial. The wrong fix was to reword the copy so the checker would go quiet, which would have removed a true and load-bearing disclaimer to satisfy a defective instrument.
theCheckerCaughtSomethingRealOnItsFirstR.fixApplied: The token list was split. HARD tokens remain presence-shaped, because there is no legitimate sentence containing 'nationwide' or 'WorkOS' in this listing. CLAIM tokens are now polarity-aware: the predicate reads the token AND whether a negator sits within the 40 characters before it. Four fixtures were added, two must-fail and two must-pass, so the polarity logic itself has positive-space coverage and not only negative-space.
theCheckerCaughtSomethingRealOnItsFirstR.residualWeakness: The 40-character negation window is a heuristic and will mis-read a long clause that negates from further away, or a double negative. It fails toward flagging, which is the safe direction: a false flag costs a read, a missed assertion costs a false public claim.

adversarialReviewOfTheCopy.attack: Read the description as a hostile buyer who will connect and immediately test the biggest promise. What is the first thing that breaks?
adversarialReviewOfTheCopy.answer: The buildable envelope. It is the most attractive phrase in the copy and it declined on the one parcel this lane probed, with declineReason atom_path_pending.
adversarialReviewOfTheCopy.resolution: The copy does not promise an envelope. It says the connector shows 'where the setbacks and buildable envelope stand', and then the honesty paragraph says outright that on many parcels the envelope is a declared refusal rather than a distance. A buyer who tests it and gets a refusal has been told in advance, which converts the weakest specimen into the demonstration of the differentiator. Basis for that framing is _smartsite_gtm/01: 'The campaign leads with it rather than apologizing for it.'
adversarialReviewOfTheCopy.residual: 'On many parcels' is unquantified. This lane did NOT measure the envelope refusal rate and deliberately used no number, because _smartsite_gtm/01 carries a 2026-08-30 measurement with an explicit instruction to re-measure before external use, and this lane did not re-measure. An unquantified 'many' is the honest form of an unmeasured rate.

adversarialReviewOfTheCopy.attack: The listing says the connector is on every plan including Free. What does a Free user actually get before they hit a wall?
adversarialReviewOfTheCopy.answer: find_parcel, list_my_properties, the four screen and save writes. get_smart_site at depth node and run_report both need a paid rung. So a free user can find parcels, keep lists and save them, and cannot open a full parcel read.
adversarialReviewOfTheCopy.riskInTheCopy: A reader could infer 'available on every plan including Free' means the useful part is free. The next sentence bounds it explicitly: opening a parcel's full read needs Solo or above or a 30-day unlock, and reading the report needs a paid plan. Card item 3 asks for exactly that pairing, that the listing not imply the connector is paid, and not imply everything inside it is free. Both halves are present in adjacent sentences rather than split across the document.
adversarialReviewOfTheCopy.unverified: The free-tier refusal was NOT observed. This lane ran on a paid account. The gate is stated in the product's own words from the deployed disclosure and read at source, but nobody has watched a free account receive upgrade_required from the connector.

adversarialReviewOfTheCopy.attack: Is there a sentence in the copy that will be false in a week?
adversarialReviewOfTheCopy.answer: Two candidates were removed by construction. The tier sentence states the invariant, 'it applies the same limits the app applies', so P-101 moving screens to Studio cannot falsify it. No tool count appears, so adding a tool cannot falsify it. The remaining exposure is capability REMOVAL or RENAME, which is precisely what happened twice in the five days before this lane ran: ask_the_map went to blocked and export_instrument stopped functioning, and both were named as live capabilities in the 2026-08-28 draft.
adversarialReviewOfTheCopy.conclusion: The copy is drift-resistant on addition and drift-fragile on removal, and no mechanism watches for removal. Stated as such in the pack and in the close rather than implied away.

adversarialReviewOfTheCopy.attack: Every capability sentence must map to a tool live and reachable at the tier the sentence implies. Walk them.
walk: 'Find a parcel by address or parcel id' -> find_parcel query, auth only, PROBED live, returned 48021:34137.

'every parcel within a set distance of one' -> find_parcel near, auth only, PROBED live after this walk flagged it as the weakest claim: 300 ft around 48021:34137 at cap 5 returned five hits with distanceFt and truncated: true, so the copy's truncation clause is earned rather than assumed.
'every parcel on a named street in a named city' -> find_parcel street. CUT FROM THE COPY. See the street-mode finding below.

'Open a parcel's on-record facts ... each carrying its citation and the date it was baked' -> get_smart_site depth node, PROBED live. Citation present on zoning. bakedAt present. NOTE: the flood section returned citationsDegraded true, meaning a present claim with no verifiable https citation, so 'each carrying its citation' is generous. See the next row.
'Read the property intelligence report for a parcel' -> run_report, paid, PROBED live, reportKind R1-baked-snapshot.

'Build a screening board from a pasted list' -> create_screen and add_to_screen, NOT probed because they write into the operator's account. list_screens WAS probed and returned 30 screens, which is indirect evidence the write path has been exercised repeatedly by other lanes.
'Save parcels, set a status on them, and list what you have saved' -> save_property and set_property_status NOT probed because they write. list_my_properties NOT probed.
adversarialReviewOfTheCopy.correctionMade: APPLIED. 'each carrying its citation and the date it was baked' overstated. The live probe returned zoning with a real https citation, but flood present with citations: [] and citationsDegraded true, which is a present claim carrying no verifiable link. The clause now reads 'carrying their citations where a source can be linked, and the date each was baked'. Description moved from 1,757 to 1,787 characters against a 2,000 cap; the checker was re-run and still exits 0. This was the only sentence in the copy where a buyer checking a real parcel could have caught us.

adversarialReviewOfTheCopy.attack: Card item 4 says any sentence not traceable to a master gets removed or routed, never written fresh. Did anything get written fresh?
adversarialReviewOfTheCopy.answer: Three sentences are not traceable to a master and all three are routed rather than quietly shipped. (1) The six-county enumeration, which contradicts the masters coverage rule and is routed as F7 with both variants supplied. (2) 'the property intelligence report', which is the deployed server's own phrase and not a master term; the masters call the deep read the X-ray and this lane could not establish that the connector's R1 read is that artifact, so it did not assert the brand name on this surface. (3) The refusal vocabulary, 'reported absent, unknown, not read, or refused', which comes from the live wire vocabulary block rather than from a master, because the master phrase 'not verified' is not a string this connector returns.
adversarialReviewOfTheCopy.judgement: All three are defensible and all three are named. None was invented; each is either a live product string or a tracked GTM doc.

adversarialReviewOfTheCopy.attack: What did the lane leave out that a competitor listing would include, and is leaving it out a mistake?
adversarialReviewOfTheCopy.answer: The MCP App panel. Three tools mount an interactive Smart Site board in the conversation, which is genuinely differentiating and is the thing a screenshot carousel would sell. It is absent from the description because this lane verified the panel's REGISTRATION in source and never watched it render. Promising a panel nobody in this lane saw is the defect class card item 2 forbids.
adversarialReviewOfTheCopy.consequence: If the operator files as an MCP App, the panel is the subject of the required screenshots anyway, and at that point it will have been seen. The description can gain a sentence about it then, on that evidence.

adversarialReviewOfTheCopy.attack: Is the lane confusing 'the copy is ready' with 'the card is close to done'?
adversarialReviewOfTheCopy.answer: No, and the pack says so first rather than last. The copy is one of nine things a filing needs. Four of the other eight are blockers this lane cannot clear: the organization plan, the screenshots, the documentation page, and the privacy retention section. Two are operator lines: the coverage ruling and the permanent slug. One is a decision about the four refusing tools. And item 1, the cold Connect, is not closed. A close that led with finished copy would be a narrated full close over an honest partial one.

streetModeFinding.severity: second capability correction, found by probing the walk's own weakest row
streetModeFinding.what: find_parcel street mode did not return inside the host's timeout window, twice in a row.
calls: street {query: 'Pine St, Bastrop TX 78602', cap: 5} -> 'This operation was aborted'
street {query: 'Pine St, Bastrop TX 78602', cap: 3} -> 'This operation was aborted'
streetModeFinding.control: near {query: '48021:34137', radiusFt: 300, cap: 5} was issued immediately afterwards and returned five hits at once. The service was warm and answering, so this is not a cold start and not a general outage.
streetModeFinding.mechanism: The street path is a bounded contains scan over county situs rows and appears not to complete inside the host's tool-call window for this query.
streetModeFinding.alternativeMechanismNotExcluded: A transport-level abort unrelated to server work. This lane cannot discriminate from the client side: the abort is client-observed and the server's own vocabulary names that class open_did_not_reach_me, 'Client-side only ... no tool result within the host's timeout window', explicitly making no claim about the underlying record. Reported as two failed attempts with a warm control, NOT as a server defect.
streetModeFinding.actionTaken: The clause naming street search was cut from the description and the street example prompt was replaced with a proven near prompt. Card item 2 requires a capability to be live AND reachable, and reachable is the half that failed.
streetModeFinding.handBack: Worth a look by the owning seat. It is also the same symptom class the 2026-08-28 blocker card recorded as a first-call abort and attributed to a scale-to-zero cold start. That attribution is now doubtful: min-instances=1 is in place, five health reads averaged under 0.5s, and a near call succeeded seconds after two street aborts. Same symptom, different cause, and the earlier explanation would have closed the question.

cardItemGrades.title: Re-prove the connect path live, from a cold client
cardItemGrades.basis: The full pre-authorization handshake was proven from a client holding no credentials: POST /mcp returned 401 carrying WWW-Authenticate with resource_metadata, the protected-resource document resolved and named the authorization server, and the authorization-server document returned S256 PKCE and its endpoints. Two negative tests confirmed a garbage bearer and a wrong scheme are both refused with distinct reasons and no fall-through. What is NOT proven is browser OAuth consent by an account that has never authorized Smart Site, followed by a first tool call. The tool calls in this lane ran through an already-authorized connector, which the card explicitly excludes. Needs a human at a browser with a fresh account.

cardItemGrades.title: The listing claims only what the connector serves
cardItemGrades.grade: PASS, and it changed the answer twice
cardItemGrades.basis: The claim-to-tool-to-gate table is in the pack. Two capability corrections came out of probing rather than reading. export_instrument does not function in production, so the not-ready set is four tools and not three and the whole export story left the copy. find_parcel street mode did not return in two attempts against a warm service, so street search left the copy too. A machine-checkable guard now exists and has been shown to fail on the exact sentence the prior draft would have shipped.

cardItemGrades.title: Tier honesty
cardItemGrades.basis: The copy carries both halves in adjacent sentences: the door is on every plan including Free, and the two paid boundaries are named in the product's own words. The free-tier refusal itself was not observed; this lane ran paid.

cardItemGrades.title: Claims come from the masters
cardItemGrades.basis: Per-sentence provenance table in the pack. Three untraceable sentences are named and routed, one of them a direct masters conflict.

cardItemGrades.title: Submitted, and the submission recorded
cardItemGrades.grade: NOT CLOSED, and cannot be closed by this lane

cardItemGrades.title: A check that fails when the listing goes stale
cardItemGrades.basis: No mechanism exists. Stated in the pack and the close as an absence with its consequence, not implied away. The copy was written to be drift-resistant on addition, which is mitigation and not a control. The shape of a real control is named and is a separate row.

recommendationBeforeFiling: The 22-character citation fix is already applied; nothing owed there.
Get the coverage ruling and the slug from the operator, one line each.

Clear the four blockers in the pack in this order: organization plan first, because it gates everything; then the privacy retention section, which is two paragraphs on a page that already exists; then the documentation page, which is a known shape; then the screenshots, which are the largest piece.
Rule the four refusing tools before a reviewer meets them.
Only then run the cold Connect from a fresh account and close item 1 with the transcript.
